title: Edgepad 4.0: the full demo and tutorial

chapters.title: What it is
lines: Laptop's plugged into the TV. You're on the couch. Your phone's already in your hand.
That's your remote now. Meet Edgepad.
It turns an Android phone into a trackpad, a remote and a control panel for your laptop. Windows, Mac or Linux.
It talks over plain Bluetooth. No account, no server, no internet.

chapters.title: Setup
lines: Setting it up takes a minute, and you only do it once.
Install the phone app, and the laptop app for your system. Both are free, on GitHub.
Pair them in your phone's Bluetooth settings, the way you'd pair a headset.
Open Edgepad and tap your laptop's name. The laptop asks if it should trust this phone. Say yes, and you're in.
Want more than a yes? Turn on a six-digit PIN, asked the first time, or every time a phone connects.

chapters.title: The trackpad
lines: The middle is a trackpad. One finger moves, and a tap clicks. Tap and hold to drag.
Two fingers scroll, and pinch to zoom.
Three fingers switch desktops. Four flip between apps.
Don't like that? Remap any gesture.

chapters.title: Corner dials
lines: Every corner is a dial that wraps around the edge. Slide for volume, brightness, zoom, or to scrub a video.
The marks light up as you go, so you can read the level at a glance.
Want more? Flip one switch, and every corner splits in two. Four dials become eight.
And it stays in sync. Turn the volume down on the laptop, and the dial follows.

chapters.title: Now playing
lines: Whatever's playing lives right on the pad. Play, pause, skip, and drag it wherever you want.

chapters.title: Lock
lines: Phone going in your pocket? Lock the trackpad, and only the dials stay live.

chapters.title: Controls
lines: Everything else is one tap away, in Controls.
A full keyboard, with Control, Alt and Shift you can hold or tap.
A gamepad the laptop sees as a real Xbox controller, on Windows and Linux.
Annotate turns your phone into a pen on the laptop's screen. Draw, highlight, add arrows and boxes, then clear it all.
Switch on Sign, write your signature, and it's saved as an image, ready for any document.
And Capture grabs a region, the full screen, or a recording, with the laptop's own tools.

chapters.title: Macros
lines: Up to fifteen macros. Apps, sites, scripts, one tap away.
They sit in a clean deck. Press and hold to rearrange them, and pick the grid that suits you.
Or skip the tap. Draw a shape on the trackpad to fire one.

chapters.title: Make it yours
lines: Make it yours. Pick what each corner does, and tune how the dials feel.
Go dark or light, set your own background, and turn it sideways if that's how you hold it.

chapters.title: Who gets in
lines: Your laptop decides who gets in. Trust more than one phone, let a trusted phone take over, or forget them all from the laptop.
Windows has been run on real laptops. The Mac and Linux apps are new, and still in testing.

chapters.title: Get it
lines: No account. No server. No internet. Just your phone and your laptop.
Edgepad. Free, open source, on GitHub.
